title: Sunny Meets the Platypus | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka meets a shy duck-billed platypus at the creek edge who teaches her the beautiful art of being completely still — still as water, still as moonlight. A soothing bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The creek was whispering tonight.

Little Sunny the quokka found it by following the sound — a soft, rippling murmur threading through the evening bush.

She crept to the bank and peered through the tall grass.

There, at the water's edge, sat the most interesting creature she had ever seen.

It had dark velvety fur. A wide, flat bill like a duck's. And tiny bright eyes that seemed to see everything and nothing all at once.

A platypus.

Sunny held very still, so as not to frighten it.

But the platypus had already seen her. It blinked once, slowly. Then it did something surprising.

It simply... stayed.

It did not run. It did not dive. It sat at the water's edge, completely still, and looked at the moon's reflection shimmering in the creek.

Sunny watched. And slowly, without really meaning to, she became still too.

Her breathing slowed. Her busy little paws went quiet in her lap.

The water moved. The moonlight moved with it — tiny ripples of silver, dancing and dissolving.

But Sunny and the platypus stayed perfectly, perfectly still.

And the most wonderful thing happened.

The night grew louder. A frog called somewhere distant. A breeze came and rustled the reeds. Stars blinked on, one by one.

When you are still, Sunny discovered, the world comes to you.

Her eyes grew heavy. The creek kept whispering its soft, gentle nothing.

The platypus lowered its bill to rest against the cool grass.

Sunny let her eyes close too.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little platypus. Goodnight, little one.
